text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto disclosed that the federal and provincial governments had given the Sindh police clear instructions that Mir Murtaza Bhutto should not be intercepted or checked.
- Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev expressed his willingness to work together with Pakistan to restore peace in Afghanistan.
- The opposition and business community will observe a countrywide strike on Saturday to vent their resentment over the new taxes by the government.
- Ghinwa Bhutto, widow of Mir Murtaza Bhutto, said she would not rest until her husband's killers were unmasked and punished.

- Pakistanis are increasingly coming into focus as major campaign donors to the Democratic and Republican parties in the current election with Chicago businessman Rashid Chaudhry named repeatedly, but no one has yet suggested anything illegal.
- A modified version of the letter of intent signed last year for the IMF standby arrangement has been prepared by the government of Pakistan for the perusal of the Fund team.

- The continued expansion of the Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd (PTCL) is causing further problems in its privatisation and the government has approached the World Bank to help sell a 26 percent management stake in PTCL to a foreign investor.

- SLow, tardy and corrupt tax collecting machinery has embarrassed the government and the entire system of Central Board of Revenue needs to be revamped, said Minister of State for Finance Makhdoom Shahabuddin in an interview.
- The government is negotiating a comprehensive programme to restructure the nationalised commercial banks with the World Bank, Minister of State for Finance Makhdoom Shahabuddin said.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto said all the Bhuttos of her family had been wiped out from the political scene to eliminate the Pakistan People's Party and parliamentary democracy.
- Eleven policemen arrested in connection with the killing of Mir Murtaza Bhutto will appear in court today.

- Islamabad will be sealed on Saturday, with 7,000 personnel of the Rangers, Frontier Constabulary and Punjab Constabulary deployed and 2,000 troops on alert, to keep away Jamaat-i-Islami protesters, a police official said.
